content: 1. The safety and efficacy of efavirenz in patients weighing less than 5 kg and under 3 months of age have not been established. 2. When coadministering efavirenz with voriconazole in patients weighing more than 40 kg and older than 12 years, increase the voriconazole maintenance dose to 400 mg every 12 hours and reduce the efavirenz dose to 300 mg daily using the capsule formulation. 3. When coadministering efavirenz with rifampin in patients weighing more than 40 kg, increase the efavirenz dose to 800 mg daily. 4. No dosage adjustment is required for efavirenz in cases of renal impairment. 5. Coadministration of efavirenz with carbamazepine is contraindicated as both drugs reduce each other's levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may lead to a loss of virologic response and potential resistance to NNRTIs. A 27% decrease in carbamazepine and a 36% decrease in efavirenz area under the curve (AUC) have been observed. 6. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of cariprazine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as CYP3A4 is responsible for the formation and elimination of cariprazine's active metabolites. The net effect of CYP3A4 inducers on cariprazine exposure has not been evaluated. 7. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of cobimetinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as strong or moderate CYP3A inducers may reduce cobimetinib systemic exposure by more than 80%, significantly reducing its efficacy. 8. Efavirenz increases the levels of deuruxolitinib by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as deuruxolitinib is contraindicated with strong or moderate CYP2C9 inhibitors. 9. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as strong CYP3A4 inducers may reduce contraceptive efficacy. Women should avoid using estradiol valerate/dienogest as contraception while on efavirenz and for at least 28 days after discontinuation of the inducer. 10. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of doravirine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as coadministration with strong CYP3A inducers may reduce doravirine plasma concentrations, leading to a loss of virologic response and potential resistance. 11. Efavirenz and dronedarone both increase the QTc interval, making their combination contraindicated. 12. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as strong CYP3A inducers may reduce the therapeutic effect of elbasvir/grazoprevir. 13. Efavirenz should not be coadministered with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF as this is a complete HIV regimen and should not be combined with other antiretrovirals. 14. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of ergonovine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Efavirenz decreases the levels of etravirine by increasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as the manufacturer's prescribing information advises against combining etravirine with other NNRTIs. 16. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of fostemsavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly reduces temsavir (active moiety) plasma concentrations, potentially leading to a loss of virologic response and resistance. 17. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 18. Lefamulin increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as lefamulin is contraindicated with CYP3A substrates known to prolong the QT interval. 19. Efavirenz increases the levels of lomitapide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as lomitapide levels may increase several folds. 20. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate, and coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers is contraindicated. 21. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of lorlatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as coadministration with strong CYP3A inducers is contraindicated. Discontinue the strong CYP3A inducer for three plasma half-lives before initiating lorlatinib. 22. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as strong CYP3A inducers minimally affect lumacaftor exposure but decrease ivacaftor exposure (AUC) by 57%, potentially reducing the effectiveness of lumacaftor/ivacaftor. 23. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism and decreases its levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 24. Efavirenz and nevirapine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. This combination is contraindicated as it is associated with an increase in adverse reactions without improvement in efficacy. 25. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 26. Efavirenz decreases the levels of panobinostat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as strong CYP3A4 inducers can reduce panobinostat levels by approximately 70%, leading to treatment failure. 27. Efavirenz and posaconazole both increase the QTc interval, making their combination contraindicated. 28. Efavirenz and ranolazine both increase the QTc interval, making their combination contraindicated. 29. Efavirenz decreases the levels of rilpivirine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as rilpivirine should not be used in combination with NNRTIs. 30. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated at efavirenz doses of 400 mg/day or higher as it induces CYP3A4, resulting in decreased voriconazole levels. When coadministered, increase voriconazole oral maintenance dose to 400 mg every 12 hours and reduce efavirenz to 300 mg every 24 hours. 31. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug as coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers reduces plasma concentrations of abemaciclib and its metabolites. 32. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of abrocitinib by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug as abrocitinib is a CYP2C9 and CYP2C19 substrate, and moderate-to-strong inhibitors of these enzymes increase systemic exposure of abrocitinib and its active metabolites, potentially increasing adverse effects. 33. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of alfuzosin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of alpelisib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug as coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended. 35. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of amiodarone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Efavirenz and amisulpride both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug, and ECG monitoring is recommended if coadministered. 37. Efavirenz and anagrelide both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of efavirenz by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug as apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, reduces exposure to CYP3A4 substrates. Evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect if coadministration is necessary. 39. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of apremilast by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug as coadministration with strong CYP inducers significantly decreases systemic exposure of apremilast, potentially resulting in loss of efficacy. 40. Efavirenz and artemether both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug as coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers decreases serum concentrations and antimalarial efficacy. 42. Efavirenz and asenapine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of atazanavir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Efavirenz and atidarsagene autotemcel should not be coadministered. Avoid or use an alternative drug as antiretroviral medications may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. Discontinue antiretrovirals for at least one month before cell mobilization or the expected duration for elimination of the medications. 45. Efavirenz decreases the levels of atovaquone by an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 46. Efavirenz decreases the levels of axitinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, and select concomitant medications with no or minimal CYP3A4 induction potential. 47. Efavirenz and azithromycin both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of bedaquiline by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug as coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers may reduce therapeutic effect. Both drugs increase the QTc interval. 49. Efavirenz and betibeglogene autotemcel should not be coadministered. Avoid or use an alternative drug as antiretroviral medications may interfere with the manufacturing of apheresis cells. Discontinue antiretrovirals for at least one month before mobilization or until all cycles of apheresis are completed. 50. Efavirenz decreases the levels of bosutinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug as strong CYP3A4 inducers decrease bosutinib plasma concentration by approximately 85%. 51. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of brigatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug as coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers may decrease brigatinib efficacy. 52. Efavirenz increases the levels of bromocriptine by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug as competitive inhibition of CYP3A4 may lead to vasospasm and ischemia. 53. Efavirenz and buprenorphine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 54. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of buprenorphine transdermal by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug as both drugs increase the QTc interval. 55. Efavirenz increases the levels of cabergoline by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug as competitive inhibition of CYP3A4 may lead to vasospasm and ischemia. 56. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of cabozantinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug as coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended. If required, increase cabozantinib dose by 40 mg/day (Cometriq) or 20 mg/day (Cabometyx) and resume the previous dose 2-3 days after discontinuation of the strong CYP3A4 inducer. 57. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of capivasertib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug as strong or moderate CYP3A inducers decrease capivasertib exposure, potentially reducing efficacy. 58. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of capmatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 59. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of carvedilol by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 60. Efavirenz decreases the levels of ceritinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 61. Efavirenz and chloroquine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 62. Efavirenz and chlorpromazine both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 63. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of citalopram by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 64. Efavirenz and clarithromycin both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
